lead: Obstetric abdominal examination on a patient or model: prepare, general look, inspection, fundal height, Leopold grips, engagement, liquor and the fetal heart, then present eight points.
f: Doppler or Pinard, gel, tape, gloves · empty bladder (a full one adds about 3 cm) · lying with a pillow under her right hip (left tilt 15°) after 20 wk · expose from xiphisternum to symphysis

sc: Dizzy, pale and sweaty flat on her back → Supine hypotension: tilt her left

f: Well or distressed · pallor (eyelid, palms) · BP, pulse, temperature, urine · pitting oedema, varicose veins
Size, shape (oval = longitudinal, broad = transverse) · scars: Pfannenstiel (lower segment CS), midline (classical CS, laparotomy) · linea nigra, striae · fetal movements
Centre the uterus, find the fundus with the side of the hand, then tape · 12 wk symphysis · 20 wk umbilicus · 36 wk xiphisternum · SFH = weeks ± 2 cm from 24 wk · off dates by > 2 cm → growth scan
Fundal: what is in the fundus · lateral: back or limbs · Pawlik (1st pelvic): what presents · pelvic (2nd, facing her feet): engagement

sc: Hard round ballotable mass in the fundus → Breech
Fundus and pelvis empty, broad uterus → Transverse lie

f: Head in fifths: ≤ 2/5 palpable = engaged · hands converge below the head = not engaged · tense uterus with a fluid thrill = polyhydramnios; parts felt too easily = oligohydramnios
Pinard or Doppler over the anterior shoulder (back side) · count 1 min with her pulse · normal 110–160/min · heard above the umbilicus = breech
Cover her, thank, wash hands · present: SFH, lie, presentation, engagement, position, liquor, fetal heart, impression

tr: Forgetting the tilt, the bladder or the chaperone loses easy marks
